Read [`./INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md`](./INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md) for the full step-by-step flow (keyless memory, optional API capabilities, maintenance, verification). ## Memory operating protocol **Which gbrain call for which lookup.** Details and caveats: [brain-first](skills/conventions/brain-first.md#which-gbrain-call-for-which-lookup). Ask gbrain before you `grep`, `cat`, `ls` or run SQL on the brain checkout: it reads the index across every source, ranks, filters and names the slug to read next. With the gbrain MCP server connected, call the tool of the same name instead of the CLI (one connection, no per-call startup). | Lookup | CLI | MCP tool | |---|---|---| | Find a page by name or path | `gbrain find [--type T] [--source S]` | `find_pages` | | Count pages by kind or source | `gbrain stats --by source,type [--since 30d] [--collapse-aliases]` | `get_stats` (needs an admin-scope token) | | Answer a question, search a topic | `gbrain query "" [--types '["meeting"]'] [--since 30d]` | `query` | | Pages with these words | `gbrain search "" [--match keyword] [--source S]` | `search` | | Read a known page | `gbrain get ` | `get_page` | | Read only the part a search hit points at | `gbrain get --around-chunk-id ` or `--lines '{"from":1,"count":200}'` | `get_page` | | What the brain knows about a person or company | `gbrain entity `, then `gbrain recall "" --json` | `entity`, `recall` | | Links, dated events, every page of a type | `gbrain backlinks `, `gbrain timeline `, `gbrain list --type T` | `get_backlinks`, `get_timeline`, `list_pages` | | Save a fact the user stated | `gbrain remember "" --entity --content-origin user_said --provenance ""` | `remember` | | Why a page didn't rank | `gbrain query "" --explain-target ` | `query` | | Which installed skill fits a request | `gbrain skills resolve --text "" --json` (after `gbrain skills index build`) | none (CLI only) | | Find something archived to B2, Supabase or S3 | `gbrain storage-find ""` | `storage_find` | Parse `--json` output instead of matching the text; notices go to stderr. Never send stderr to `/dev/null`: a refusal there (`no_brain`, `GBRAIN_DB_ACCESS`) then reads as "no results"; check the exit code too. Take `chunk_id` from a fresh `search --json` hit (an old one fails `revision_changed`), and read a degraded notice before concluding the brain has nothing. Recall relevant saved context before answering. Resolve a person (an email sender, an attendee) only by an exact match (`gbrain whois `), never a search's top hit ([identity rule](skills/conventions/brain-first.md#identity-exact-match)). Save explicit requests to remember with provenance; confirm corrections against the stored record. Automatic capture requires opt-in; the [conversation archive](docs/guides/conversation-archive.md) (one redacted page per conversation per day) is on by default on a personal brain and off with `gbrain transcripts archive off`. Withdrawal (`forget`) removes a fact from active memory; history, source material, and private backups may remain. Never promise physical erasure. Verify changes with actual GBrain calls and distinguish a local test from a new-conversation test in the harness. Durable preferences and facts belong in shared memory when the user wants them recalled later. Transient task state, credentials, local configuration, and harness activation state do not. Remote `put_page` saves references as text without inline graph extraction; a post-commit `links` effect then adds plain mention edges to existing pages the writer can see (`mcp.remote_auto_links`, on by default). Typed edges rely on stdio's best-effort startup/idle sweeps, explicit host maintenance or authorized `add_link` calls. Configured model providers can receive text; Markdown export is not a full database backup. Read [memory boundaries](docs/guides/memory-boundaries.md) before promising portability, graph freshness, privacy, or recovery. ## Multi-agent rules for a shared brain checkout Several agents, crons and hooks often commit to one brain checkout on the same machine. In such a checkout: 1. **Commit and push with one command, naming your files:** `scripts/brain-commit-push.sh "" `, or `gbrain git commit-push -m "" -- ` when the brain has no helper. It takes the checkout's writer lock, commits only those paths, merges remote commits without touching anyone else's files, and fails loudly if the push does not land. 2. **Bring remote commits in with `--pull`** (`scripts/brain-commit-push.sh --pull` or `gbrain git commit-push --pull`) at session start and before a batch of writes. 3. **On a non-zero exit, read the code.** Retry once on `commit_lock_busy`. Stop and relay to the user on `integrate_conflict` (they choose which version wins) and on `writer_coordinator_required` (a managed brain: save pages with `put_page` instead). `pushed_checkout_lagging` is a success. 4. **Never run** `git pull --rebase`, `git stash`, `--autostash`, `git add -A`, `git commit -a`, `git reset --hard` or `git push --force` there, and never fall back to them when the command fails. Never delete `.git/rebase-merge` before saving its autostash with `git stash store`. Outcomes, conflict recovery, a stuck rebase and the lock contract for host daemons: [docs/guides/shared-checkout-git.md](docs/guides/shared-checkout-git.md). ## Agent operator protocol Every gbrain error, refusal, degraded result and recommendation carries the same machine contract. The quick version: 1. Read `code` (fall back to `error` on older servers). `message` says what happened, `why` says why. 2. Follow `fix.next`: - `run` → run `fix.argv` (CLI) or call `fix.mcp` (MCP) exactly as given. - `ask_user` → relay `user_message` to the user and stop; run the fix only after they agree. - `tell_user_to_run` → give the user `fix.command`; it needs them or the brain host's operator. - `wait` → retry after the stated delay with the same request. - `report` → tell the user what happened and run `gbrain doctor --json`. 3. A degraded result is not proof of "no notes": a result stamped `[gbrain degraded: …]` (`_meta.degraded`, the CLI `degraded` key) is partial. Exit 3 always means "stop and ask the user". Exit 10 means the write was accepted and is still pending: never "not found" or "failed", so poll the receipt (`gbrain write-request `) before retrying, reporting or moving on. [`./skills/RESOLVER.md`](./skills/RESOLVER.md) — skill dispatcher. Read before any task. ## Trust boundary (critical) GBrain distinguishes **trusted local CLI callers** (`OperationContext.remote = false`, set by `src/cli.ts`) from **untrusted agent-facing callers** (`remote = true`, set by `src/mcp/server.ts`). Security-sensitive operations like `file_upload` tighten filesystem confinement when `remote = true` and default to strict behavior when unset. If you are writing or reviewing an operation, consult `src/core/operations.ts` for the contract. ## Common tasks - **Configure:** [`docs/ENGINES.md`](./docs/ENGINES.md), [`docs/guides/live-sync.md`](./docs/guides/live-sync.md), [`docs/mcp/DEPLOY.md`](./docs/mcp/DEPLOY.md), [`docs/guides/remote-mcp.md`](./docs/guides/remote-mcp.md) (`gbrain mcp expose`). - **Run gbrain from cron, workspace scripts and hooks:** every caller goes through one wrapper that sets `GBRAIN_HOME` (never `HOME`), loads the brain's env file and runs the installed binary, never `bun run src/cli.ts` with an inherited environment. ```bash

```bash
gbrain extract links --source db                         # commit
gbrain extract timeline --source db                      # dated events
gbrain stats                                             # verify links > 0
```

For brand-new empty brains, skip this backfill: there is nothing to extract yet.

and HTTP MCP) saves references as text without inline graph extraction; a
post-commit `links` effect then adds plain mention edges to existing pages the
writer can see (`gbrain config set mcp.remote_auto_links off` disables it). Stdio

check and can leave a release the host's Bun cannot start. When the floor is
above the host's Bun, the upgrade refuses with `requires Bun >=<floor>` and
changes nothing (exit 78): run `bun upgrade`, then the same upgrade command
again. Pass `--no-bun-floor-check` only after checking the target yourself
when the floor cannot be read (offline). See
[Bun floor](docs/guides/upgrades-auto-update.md#bun-floor).

postinstall hooks; it does not skip other migrations. Keep the environment form
on the package-manager command because hooks run before `post-upgrade`.
`GBRAIN_NO_REEMBED=1` separately skips the potentially paid reindex step.

assuming memory-only options are the desired maintenance policy. Verify a known
keyword query after upgrading, not just the version string.

## The onboard surface

`gbrain onboard` is gbrain's activation surface.
Once your brain has any content, run `gbrain onboard --check --json` to
see structured recommendations across 5 brain-health axes (orphans,
stale embeddings, entity link coverage, timeline coverage, takes count).

**On first connect (after `gbrain init`):**
```bash
gbrain onboard --check --json
```
The JSON envelope (`schema_version: 1`) carries `recommendations[]` with
`apply_policy` per item: `auto_apply` (safe to run unattended),
`prompt_required` (needs explicit user consent), or `manual_only`
(pack upgrade, paid takes bootstrap: the user runs it).

**After every `gbrain upgrade`:**
```bash
gbrain onboard --check --json
```
New versions may surface new opportunities. The post-upgrade banner
nudges the user when it runs, but agents should re-probe as a hygiene
step regardless.

**Unattended remediation (cron / autopilot):**
```bash
gbrain onboard --auto --max-usd 5
```
Refuses without `--max-usd N`. Never runs `manual_only` items; it
lists them in `manual_only_skipped`. The autopilot daemon also consults
onboard recommendations on its tick — no explicit agent action needed
for the autonomous path.

brain health + drive remediation over OAuth-authenticated MCP. Protected
LLM-bearing handlers (synthesize, patterns, consolidate, takes-bootstrap,

scope — admin alone is insufficient. The MCP op returns
`skipped_missing_scope[]` listing what would have run with the right
grants.

- Autopilot's auto-apply tier for takes-bootstrap is `manual_only`

**Suppress nudges in CI / scripted environments:**
```bash
export GBRAIN_NO_ONBOARD_NUDGE=1
```

Init and upgrade notices do not skip themselves when there is no terminal:

{"content": "1|# Connect GBrain to Hermes
2|
3|> This page is the MCP-registration reference for Hermes (the NousResearch
4|> `hermes-agent`). For the full brain install — CLI, engine, skills, dream
5|> cycle — follow [INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md](../../INSTALL_FOR_AGENTS.md) first;
6|> this page wires the finished brain into Hermes over stdio MCP.
7|
8|Hermes spawns `gbrain serve` as a local stdio subprocess. No server, no tunnel,
9|no token needed. Works with both PGLite and Supabase engines. No machine that
10|stays online? Hosted GBrain at [gbrain.io](https://gbrain.io/?ref=hermes-md) is always on.
11|
12|## Register (recommended)
13|
14|```bash
15|printf 'Y\n' | hermes mcp add gbrain --env GBRAIN_HOME=$HOME --connect-timeout 60 --command $(which gbrain) --args serve --surface starter --advertise verbs
16|```
17|
18|The tool list shows the seven memory verbs (`recall`, `remember`, `entity`, …)
19|plus `request_tools`; every other operation stays callable, and `request_tools`
20|lists it and returns its schema. Drop `--advertise verbs` to list every
21|operation.
22|
23|`hermes mcp add` performs a real MCP handshake and tool discovery at add time,
24|then prompts `Enable all N tools? [Y/n/select]:`. Three gotchas, all observed:
25|
26|- **`--args` must be the LAST option.** Everything after it — including a
27|  misplaced `--env` — is swallowed into the server argv. To pass several
28|  environment variables, list them all after ONE `--env` flag
29|  (`--env A=1 B=2`); repeating the flag replaces the earlier values and the
30|  server is saved disabled when its handshake then fails. Put `--env` and
31|  `--connect-timeout` before `--command`, exactly as above.
32|- **Pipe the `Y` in non-interactive contexts.** EOF on the enable-tools prompt
33|  prints `Cancelled.` and saves nothing. The piped `Y` saves the server with
34|  all tools enabled.
35|- **The exit code is 0 even on connection failure or cancel.** Never assert on
36|  `mcp add`'s exit status — verify with `hermes mcp list` and
37|  `hermes mcp test gbrain` (below).
38|
39|## Brain-first instructions
40|
41|Registering the MCP server only makes the tools available. Agents seldom call a
42|brain nobody told them about, so finish the install with:
43|
44|```bash
45|gbrain setup hermes --instructions-only
46|```
47|
48|It writes one short marked block into `$HERMES_HOME/SOUL.md` (default `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`), after your identity
49|text, which stays first and unchanged: before answering any turn,
50|search the brain first, read the best hit, fill gaps with other tools, apply your own
51|access rules, then finish the task. Text outside the markers is never touched, a
52|re-run upgrades the block in place, `--dry-run` previews it,
53|`--no-instructions` opts out (and is remembered) and `--remove` takes it out.
54|`gbrain doctor` warns when the block is missing or out of date. Setup never
55|creates `SOUL.md`: Hermes uses a non-empty one instead of its default identity,
56|so start Hermes once (it seeds the file) or write your identity there first.
57|
58|The same rule also rides every turn. Setup appends a marked `pre_llm_call` shell
59|hook to `$HERMES_HOME/config.yaml` and records its approval in Hermes's
60|`shell-hooks-allowlist.json` for that exact command:
61|
62|```yaml
63|hooks:
64|  pre_llm_call:
65|    - command: "/bin/echo '{\"context\":\"GBrain: before answering this turn, check GBrain first ...\"}'"
66|      timeout: 10
67|```
68|
69|The command is self-contained: it echoes the rule as Hermes's `{"context": ...}`
70|wire shape, starts no gbrain process and needs no path on the Hermes host but
71|`/bin/echo`. Hermes appends that context to each user message, so the rule
72|reaches the model next to the turn instead of only in the system prompt. Text
73|outside the markers is never touched, and a re-run after an upgrade rewrites the
74|command and moves its approval. When config.yaml already has a `hooks:` section,
75|setup prints the entry to add yourself instead; approve it when Hermes asks (or
76|set `HERMES_ACCEPT_HOOKS=1`). `hermes hooks doctor` checks it: setup runs it
77|when `hermes` is on PATH and exits non-zero with `turn_hook_not_loaded` when the
78|hook is not healthy ([repair](../guides/repair.md#turn-hook-not-loaded)).
79|`--no-instructions` and `--remove` take the hook and its approval out.
80|
81|Hermes lists gbrain's tools only inside `tool_search`'s description, so with an
82|MCP connection the rule also names them (`mcp__gbrain__recall`, `mcp__gbrain__entity`
83|and the rest) and says to find them with `tool_search`.
84|
85|Search results also carry `_meta.brain_hot_memory`, the brain's recent facts.
86|Hermes may pass them to the model; they can include other sessions' facts, so
87|see [the channel's contract](../protocol/MCP_META_CHANNELS.md#brain_hot_memory)
88|before relying on them.
89|
90|## Direct config (equally supported)
91|

208|### Setting and resolving the mode
209|
210|```bash
211|gbrain config set search.mode tokenmax
212|```
213|
214|Per-knob resolution (highest first):

216|    per-call SearchOpts → per-key config override (search.cache.enabled, …) →
217|      MODE_BUNDLES[search.mode] → MODE_BUNDLES.balanced (fallback)
218|
219|Mode resolution lives in bare `hybridSearch`, not just the cached wrapper,
220|so eval replays test the same mode-affected behavior as the production
221|`query` op. Result counts follow the per-call `limit`, or the mode's
222|`searchLimit` when no limit is supplied. The wrapper does not read or write
223|stored semantic results while caching is disabled. `gbrain search modes`
224|reports effective `cache_enabled: false`, and `cache stats` reports
225|`enabled: false`, even when retained configuration enables the cache.

227|### Cost intuition
228|
229|The table estimates only the tokens your *downstream agent* pays to read
230|per query: an assumed payload per mode times 10K queries a month times the
231|model's input rate from gbrain's pricing table (`src/core/model-pricing.ts`).
232|Embedding, reranking and expansion calls are separate charges. The
233|corner-to-corner spread is about 200x once you pair mode with downstream model.
234|The install picker and the upgrade banner print the same matrix from
235|`src/core/search/mode-advice.ts`.

237|| Mode \ Downstream | Haiku 5.5 (\$0.10/M in) | Sonnet 5.5 (\$2/M in) | Opus 5.5 (\$4/M in) |
238||---|---|---|---|
239|| conservative (~4K tok) | **\$4/mo** | \$80/mo | \$160/mo |
240|| balanced (~10K tok) | \$10/mo | \$200/mo | \$400/mo |
241|| tokenmax (~20K tok) | \$20/mo | \$400/mo | **\$800/mo** |

244|semantic result caching is disabled; repeated searches may take longer and use
245|more provider calls. Downstream prompt caching in the agent loop is independent.
246|Mismatched pairings waste capacity in both directions — a tokenmax payload overwhelms a cheap model,
247|a conservative payload starves an expensive one. The full methodology and
248|realistic-scale walkthrough live in

259|gbrain search diagnose "<query>" --target <slug>
260|                                 # trace where a page surfaces (or fails to)
261|                                 # across the keyword/vector/alias/hybrid layers
262|```

309|## Query instruction prefix
310|
311|Instruction-style embedding models (Qwen3-Embedding, e5, BGE v1.5, nomic-embed, EmbeddingGemma)
312|expect a query instruction in front of each search query and none in front of
313|documents. GBrain sends no instruction unless you set one for the brain;
314|nothing is guessed from the model id at query time. `gbrain doctor` reports
315|`embedding_query_prefix` when the configured model belongs to one of those
316|families and no prefix is set, and prints the model card's value as a command
317|you can run as printed.
318|
319|| Family | Documented value |
320||---|---|
321|| Qwen3-Embedding | `Instruct: Given a web search query, retrieve relevant passages that answer the query` + newline + `Query:` |
322|| e5 | `query: ` |
323|| BGE v1.5 | `Represent this sentence for searching relevant passages: ` |
324|| nomic-embed | `search_query: ` |
325|| EmbeddingGemma | `task: search result \| query: ` |
326|
327|**Set.** Quote the value so trailing spaces and newlines survive the shell;
328|a newline needs ANSI-C quoting:
329|
330|```bash
331|gbrain config set embedding_query_prefix "query: "
332|gbrain config set embedding_query_prefix $'Instruct: Given a web search query, retrieve relevant passages that answer the query\nQuery:'
333|```
334|
335|The prefix is stored in the brain's database config, so each brain (and each
336|mounted brain in one MCP server) uses its own. It applies to query embeddings
337|only: keyword search uses the original query, stored document vectors are not
338|re-embedded, and the query-cache key includes the prefix. It takes effect on
339|the next CLI or MCP query without restarting a running server.
340|
341|**Verify.** `gbrain config get embedding_query_prefix --raw` prints the stored
342|bytes, and `gbrain doctor` stops reporting `embedding_query_prefix`.
343|
344|**Unset.** `gbrain config unset embedding_query_prefix` restores bare query
345|embeddings on the next query.
346|
347|nomic-embed also expects `search_document: ` in front of documents, and
348|EmbeddingGemma's card formats documents as `title: {title} | text: {text}`.
349|GBrain does not prefix or format documents, so on those models the query prefix
350|is a partial fix (#3783, #5215).
351|
352|## Choosing a lookup verb (search vs query vs get)
353|
354|Independent of which bundle is active, every individual lookup should use
355|the cheapest verb that answers the question.
356|
357|```
358|on user_asks_about(topic):
359|    # Decision tree: pick the right lookup verb
360|
361|    if know_exact_slug(topic):
362|        # Direct get -- instant, no search overhead
363|        result = gbrain get <slug>
364|        # e.g., "Tell me about Alice" -> gbrain get alice-example
365|        # Returns the FULL page -- compiled truth + timeline
366|
367|    elif topic.is_exact_name or topic.is_keyword:
368|        # MODE 1: Cheap-hybrid search -- vector + keyword + RRF, NO LLM
369|        # expansion. Embeds the query when embeddings are configured; the
370|        # keyword arm still works day-one without them (keyword-only is
371|        # also available via the search.mcp_keyword_only opt-out).
372|        results = gbrain search "{name_or_keyword}"
373|        # e.g., "Find anything about Series A" -> gbrain search "Series A"
374|        # Returns CHUNKS, not full pages
375|
376|        # IMPORTANT: search returns chunks
377|        # If the chunk confirms relevance, THEN load the full page:
378|        if chunk.confirms_relevance:
379|            full_page = gbrain get <slug_from_chunk>
380|
381|    elif topic.is_semantic_question or topic.is_concept_or_landscape:
382|        # MODE 2: Full hybrid -- vector + keyword + RRF + reranking. Owns
383|        # concept / landscape / "all-of-X" questions. Pass --expand to add
384|        # one LLM expansion call when the original wording is weak; it is
385|        # off by default because it measured no retrieval gain (GBRA-94).
386|        results = gbrain query "{natural language question}"
387|        # e.g., "Who do I know at fintech companies?" -> gbrain query "fintech contacts"
388|        # e.g., "all the companies doing offshore wind" -> gbrain query "..."
389|        # Returns ranked chunks via vector + keyword + RRF (+ expansion with --expand)
390|
391|        # Same rule: chunks first, then get full page if needed
392|        if chunk.confirms_relevance:
393|            full_page = gbrain get <slug_from_chunk>
394|
395|# Quick reference:
396|# | Mode        | Command              | Needs Embeddings | Speed   | Best For                                  |
397|# |-------------|----------------------|------------------|---------|-------------------------------------------|
398|# | Cheap-hybrid| gbrain search "term" | Uses if present  | Fastest | Known names, exact tokens                 |
399|# | Full hybrid | gbrain query "..."   | Yes              | Fast    | Concept / landscape / "all-of-X", synonyms |
400|# | Direct      | gbrain get <slug>    | No               | Instant | When you know the slug                    |
401|
402|# Progression over time:
403|#   Day 1:  search (keyword arm works without embeddings)
404|#   After first embed: vector arm + full hybrid (query) unlocked
405|#   Once you know slugs: direct get for speed
406|
407|# Precedence for conflicting information within a page:
408|#   1. User's direct statements (always wins)
409|#   2. Compiled truth sections (synthesized from evidence)
410|#   3. Timeline entries (raw signal, reverse chronological)
411|#   4. External sources (web search, APIs)
412|```
413|
414|### Tricky Spots
415|
416|1. **Search returns chunks, not full pages.** After `gbrain search` or `gbrain query`, you get excerpts. Always run `gbrain get <slug>` to load the full page when the chunk confirms relevance. Don't answer questions from chunks alone when the full context matters.
417|2. **Search works without embeddings.** On day one before any embedding run, `gbrain search` still works (the keyword arm carries it; the vector arm joins once embeddings exist). Don't tell the user "search isn't available yet" -- search is always available.
418|3. **Don't use full hybrid for known names.** `gbrain query "Alice Example" --expand` wastes an LLM expansion call, and bare `query` returns the larger evidence payload. Use `gbrain search "Alice Example"` or better yet `gbrain get alice-example` if you know the slug.
419|4. **Token budget awareness.** A full page via `gbrain get` can be large. Read the search chunks first to confirm relevance before pulling the full page. "Did anyone mention the Series A?" -- search results (chunks) are probably enough. "Tell me everything about Alice" -- get the full page.
420|5. **Full hybrid needs embeddings to have been run.** If `gbrain query` returns nothing but `gbrain search` finds results, the embeddings haven't been generated yet. Run the embedding pipeline first.
421|6. **A populated `gbrain search` result set is not proof you found everything.** Neither verb expands by default, so synonym- and outcome-phrased matches can be missed even when a search returns plenty of hits. For "find every / all / the landscape of" questions, use `gbrain query`, adding `--expand` (one call to the configured expansion model, which needs an expansion provider) when the wording is likely to differ from the notes; expanded results are still a ranked top-K; for literal exhaustive enumeration ("list every page of type X"), use `list_pages` pagination. A nonzero count is not a completeness signal.
422|7. **A remote `search` or `query` with no `limit` returns at most a few pages that matched only by meaning.** Over MCP (HTTP or stdio), every page that matched the query's words, a name, an alias or an exact identity comes back, but pages that only the vector arm found fill the result only up to `search.remote_page_cap` distinct pages in total (default 3). Without the cap, an embedding-backed search on a small brain returned most of the brain on every call, pages from other members' sources included. When the cap leaves pages out, a line after the results says how many (`_meta.retrieval.page_cap` counts them); pass `limit` for the full ranked list, which landscape and "find every" questions usually want. Local CLI calls, an explicit `limit`, paged calls, image queries and host-run subagent tool calls are never capped; a thin-client CLI call is remote, so it is capped and prints the line on stderr (pass `--limit`). Set the cap with `gbrain config set search.remote_page_cap <n>`; `0` turns it off.
423|
424|### How to Verify
425|
426|1. Run `gbrain search "Alice"` -- confirm it returns chunks with matching text and slug references.
427|2. Run `gbrain query "who works at fintech companies"` -- confirm it returns semantically relevant results (not just keyword matches on "fintech").
428|3. Run `gbrain get alice-example` -- confirm it returns the full page with compiled truth and timeline.
429|4. Compare: search for the same entity using all three modes. Keyword should be fastest, hybrid should surface conceptual matches, direct should return the complete page.
430|5. After a search returns a chunk, run `gbrain get` on the slug from that chunk. Confirm the full page contains more context than the chunk alone.
431|6. Run `gbrain search modes` -- confirm the active mode bundle, any per-key overrides, and the `Reranker:` line (`enabled` with the key present, or `off`) are what you expect.
